title: Box Read Across Pages (Print Only)

illustrates.quote: When a box reads across facing pages, but there is other text outside the box, place it at the most logical place on one of the two pages. Insert a transcriber’s note before the box, informing the reader of the location. Sample: The following box appears across the bottom of pages 100-101.

blocks.features: A two-panel colour worksheet spread spanning the bottom of textbook pages 188 (left) and 189 (right); both panels have a torn/jagged top edge (an illustration-clipping device, not part of the original worksheet's own border); ten small red oval icons, each containing a single bold digit 1-10, are embedded inline within the sentences as fill-in-the-blank answer markers running continuously across both panels.
Large white-on-green arrow-shaped banner heading the left panel.

items.text: Students noticed that a factory wasn't using [1] to remove ashes. Also, it didn't have bins for [2] cans.
Often people leave water running or waste it in other ways. They should know that it is expensive to clean [4], or waste water.
Food and other things we buy have a lot of packaging. This turns into garbage and other [6] that fills up [7].
The roads are crowded with cars that cause [9]. Most cars on the road have only one person in them.

blocks.features: Left panel: four rows, each a short 'problem' sentence with one or two circled-number blanks; bracketed numbers [N] stand in for the print's own small red numbered-oval icons.
Large white-on-green arrow-shaped banner heading the right panel.

items.text: They invited the factory manager to school to see their recycling project and a display showing how sunlight is turned into [3].
Suggest taking a field trip to the [5] to see how sewage is cleaned.

blocks.features: Right panel: four rows, each a short 'solution' sentence with one circled-number blank, matching the problem numbers on the left panel.

print.notes: Print-only illustrative figure captioned 'Example 7-4: Box Read Across Pages (Print Only)'. No braille transcription is given. The rule text immediately preceding this figure (7.4.1.c) includes its own generic sample transcriber's-note wording citing hypothetical 'pages 100-101' -- unrelated to this figure's own (unrelated) textbook page numbers 188/189 visible at the bottom corners of the image; a coincidence of two independent uses of page numbers, not a discrepancy.
print.surroundingText: Immediately follows rule 7.4.1.c's own text and its embedded sample transcriber's-note wording (see illustrates.quote).
print.printFeatures: Full-colour textbook-worksheet graphic; green arrow-shaped banners; light blue and white alternating text bands; small red oval number icons; torn-paper illustration top edge (clipping device, not part of the original worksheet's own border).

braille.notes: No braille given in the source -- the example is explicitly captioned '(Print Only)'; nothing but four blank lines (5515-5518) sit between the caption (5514) and the next content, rule 7.4.1.d (5519).

resolution: Content agreed identically between the two runs (worksheet sentence text byte-identical, including all ten bracketed blank numbers). Structural: A folded the panel banners ('See a Problem?'/'Find a Solution!') into each list's own free-text `features` note; B attached them as a `text` field directly on the list block. Reconciled as their own explicit `heading` sibling blocks (cell-5, `level:2`) immediately before each list, consistent with how a bold banner heading is modelled elsewhere in this section (see sample-7-02's 'STUDY' heading), rather than folding real, distinct print heading text into another block's own field. The first circled digit (ambiguous between '1'/'0' in both runs' initial read) is confirmed '1' by a fresh 250dpi crop of the PDF page image (p.189): a plain vertical unserifed stroke with no closed counter, matching the unambiguous '10' icon's own glyph style elsewhere in the same graphic -- no longer recorded as uncertain.
